claims.text: Financial support is available for individuals disseminating research on British art.
The support is for the publication of monographs, edited collections, catalogues, and articles.
Grants are tiered, with 'Small' grants up to £2,000 and 'Large' grants from £2,001 to £6,000.
Author Grants are open to individuals at any stage of their career.
Applicants must have a publisher confirmed.
Applicants must have a publication date scheduled within three years of applying.
Applications for the Autumn 2026 round of funding are open.
Applications close on Monday 14 September 2026.
Eligible costs include licensing of images, subventions, external contributors' fees, and translation costs for original materials.
The grant does not support the writing or research process.
A copy of the publication must be sent to the Paul Mellon Centre (PMC) library upon successful application.
A written final report is not required.
Applications must include a clear outline of the publication, details on how the grant enhances the publication, a comprehensive budget, and one academic or professional reference.
A letter or note of confirmation from the publisher must be uploaded.

Applications are assessed based on originality, contribution to scholarship, timeliness, geographical/cultural context, need, impact and inclusion, feasibility and quality, and value for money/environmental impact.
All applications must be submitted via grants.paul-mellon-centre.ac.uk.
The referee will be contacted directly after application submission.
Applicants are responsible for ensuring their referee submits their reference by the deadline.
There is a two-round assessment process.
Author Grants cannot be used for new or revised editions of previously published works, or translations of previously published works (unless including substantial new research or analysis).
Author Grants cannot be used for open access publishing costs.
Applications from publishers or organisations on behalf of an author are not permitted.
Individuals can only apply for one Author Grant per round.
Large text or clear text formats of application forms and guidance are available upon request.
Funding is available to help applicants who may face additional barriers and incur extra costs whilst undertaking research projects.
Successful applicants will be asked to agree to Terms and Conditions.
Successful applicants must acknowledge the support of the Paul Mellon Centre within the publication.
Applications opened on Monday 3 August 2026.
References are due by Wednesday 23 September 2026.
The first assessment round is from Thursday 24 September to Monday 19 October 2026.
The second assessment round is from Friday 23 October to Monday 23 November 2026.
Decisions will be communicated to applicants by Friday 27 November 2026.
Funding enquiries can be made via email to [email protected] or by calling 020 7580 0311.
